noAccess.title: No access to workspaces
noAccess.text: Workspaces, GPU time and JupyterHub come with projects. For most people a personal project from a budget that is approved at once is enough.

servers.title: Active workspaces
servers.intro: Your active workspaces in JupyterHub. Each active workspace ends by itself when it is not used, and at the latest after its environment's run time (see state).
servers.name: Workspace
servers.stopMessage: “{{name}}” is stopped. Files in the home stay, unsaved changes in open notebooks are lost.
servers.ends: Ends after {{idle}} without activity, in {{left}} at the latest.

usage.title: Usage
usage.hint: What workspaces reserved from {{from}} to {{to}}: workspace hours, vCPU, RAM and GPU hours, home size. Collected every minute; today is not complete yet.
usage.csvHint: The grouping shown as CSV, with the measured values.
usage.explain: What is charged is the reservation (requested cores and memory), as with flavors in OpenStack. “CPU used” relates the measured use to it. Home GB-days: space used, measured hourly, the day's largest value counts; a project's storage is listed as “Projektspeicher”.

projects.profilesFromTree: The project's budget decides its workspace types (quotas, Workspaces: “Workspace type …”); none without a grant.

image.buildOnSave: The build starts on saving (usually 5–15 minutes).
image.label: Environment
image.hint: What is installed in the project’s workspaces, the same for every workspace type. The workspace type only chooses the hardware (CPU, CPU with GPU kernel, GPU).
image.finishedHint: A publicly pullable image. Built on one of our bases (FROM registry.gpu.services.dhbw.cloud/platform/base-…) it runs with everything; any other runs as it is (it needs jupyterhub-singleuser), without “CPU + GPU kernel”.
image.notDerived: This image is not built on one of our bases: it runs as it is, without “CPU + GPU kernel” and without the DHBW extensions.
image.updateAvailable: The tag now points at a newer version. Running and new workspaces stay on the current one until it is taken.
image.autoUpdate: Take new versions of the tag automatically
image.autoUpdateHint: Otherwise a newer version is only shown and taken at the press of a button. New workspaces then start with it, running ones keep theirs.
image.gitHint: Built like Binder from requirements.txt, environment.yml, apt.txt and postBuild (top level, binder/ or .binder/) on the chosen base. The repository’s files reach the workspaces as “Material from Git” (below). A new version of the base triggers a rebuild; until a build is ready, the previous image stays.
image.baseRunsOut: {{name}} runs out. Successor: {{successor}}. The project keeps it until its end unless it is changed.
image.baseRunsOutOn: {{name}} runs out on {{date}}. The project is then moved to {{successor}} (environments built from Git are rebuilt on it).

material.title: Material from Git
material.hint: Fetched into ~/projects/<repository> and updated at every workspace start, without overwriting one’s own changes; JupyterLab opens that folder. Independent of the environment, so with an existing image too.

credentials.title: Access to private repositories and images
credentials.hint: With access to a host, the material from Git and an existing image can be private there; the project's workspaces use it when they start. The token is stored encrypted and not shown again; a new one for the same host replaces it. Builds from private repositories are not offered yet.
credentials.providers: GitHub: classic token with “repo” and “read:packages”, user name = GitHub name. GitLab: deploy token of the project or group with “read_repository” and “read_registry”, user name = the token's name (add the registry host separately, e.g. registry.gitlab.com). Forgejo/Gitea: token with “read:repository” and “read:package”.

projects.limits: Limits per person (at the same time)
projects.limitsHint: Counted is what one person runs in this project at the same time.

limit.noGpus: The project has no GPUs; GPUs are requested in the budget.

projects.budgetsHint: Tighter limits within the project quotas, e.g. at most 40 vCPU hours per person in 7 days, so nobody uses up the quota alone. Windows in calendar days: “today”, 7 or 30 days including today, “total” since the project was created. Once a limit is reached, no workspace starts and running workspaces end within 5 minutes (the home stays).
projects.profilesHint: What members can choose when starting a workspace in JupyterHub. The platform sets the list; GPU types count against the project's GPU quotas.
projects.adminOnlyHint: Workspace types, limits and usage limits are set by admins. The environment (base, project image, Git), the material and the release times (within the budget's maximums) can be changed here.

jobs.title: Batch jobs
jobs.allowHint: Commands and notebooks run as a job on one of the project's GPUs, without an open workspace.
jobs.noGpu: The project has no GPU class; GPUs are requested in the budget.
jobs.maxHours: Maximum run time of a job
jobs.preemptible: From the budget: preemptible – when a workspace needs the GPU, the job is stopped and starts over afterwards.
jobs.guaranteed: From the budget: guaranteed – workspaces do not preempt the jobs.
jobs.gpuHours: GPU hours: {{budgets}}; each job reserves GPU × maximum run time ({{hours}} h) of them when submitted.

storage.title: Storage (admins)
storage.hint: Workspace storage on JuiceFS: one volume per project with storage, plus homes from before the projects. Measured hourly.
storage.ofNode: of the node's {{total}} GB RAM · peak {{peak}} GB
storage.noReport: No measurement since the AI service last restarted; the next comes on the hour.
storage.explain: A project's limit is its workspace storage from the budget tree; a full volume refuses further writes. The metadata grow with the number of files (roughly 1 GB RAM per 2–3 million files); when RAM runs short, JuiceFS stops.

gpuHours.title: GPU use per hour
gpuHours.hint: How full the GPUs were, per hour in local time: colour = share held by workspaces; red outline = someone waited. Sampled every minute, kept 365 days.
gpuHours.hintProject: Who in the project held or waited for a GPU, and when, in the chosen period.
gpuHours.cell: {{day}}, {{hour}}:00–{{hour}}:59: workspaces {{share}}, gap filler {{inference}}, waiting on average {{avg}}, at most {{max}}
gpuHours.empty: No GPU use in this period.
gpuHours.explain: Counted is how long a GPU was assigned, not how much it computed. The gap filler (vLLM) uses a GPU as long as no workspace needs it and gives way at once. Waiting time: time in Kueue's queue until a GPU was free.

fleet.title: GPUs
fleet.intro: Every GPU node belongs to a pool (who the GPUs are for) and a tier (how large they are). Pool and tier make a GPU class: the budget tree grants it, and a workspace's start chooses it. More GPUs of an existing class need nothing in the tree; a node without pool takes no workspaces.
fleet.classesHint: Each class has its own queue and two resources in the budget tree. A class without nodes stays; its starts wait.
fleet.nodesHint: New GPU nodes appear here as soon as they are in the cluster. Changes apply to new pods within a minute; running ones stay where they are. The gap filler is an LLM that uses the GPU while no workspace needs it.
fleet.noNodes: No GPU nodes in the cluster.
fleet.poolsHint: “general” is for everybody; a pool of its own is for GPUs only certain budgets should get (grant them in the tree only there). The id becomes part of the tree resources; when it changes, the amounts in the tree move along. A pool that lends gives idle GPUs to the other pools of the same tier and takes them back as soon as it needs them.
fleet.poolIdInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, 2–20 characters
fleet.renamePoolHint: The pool's GPU classes get new ids; budgets, projects and booked GPU hours move along, the gap filler restarts once.
fleet.poolKeptClassesTip: A GPU class comes into being as soon as a node is assigned to the pool. It is a resource of the budget tree and projects may hold budget for it; that is why classes and their pool stay, even without nodes.

start.title: Start workspace
start.intro: Choose project and environment. The choice is in this page's address: a link with project and environment can go to all members of the project.
start.introSingle: Choose the environment; the project is set, as it is the only one a workspace can start in. The choice is in this page’s address: a link with project and environment can go to all members of the project.
start.booked: Computing time is booked to this project.
start.storage: The home directory belongs to the project ({{gb}} GB for all members together) and is the same in every environment; its folder project-shared is for all members. Deleting the project deletes these files too.
start.noStorage: This project has no workspace storage: files are lost when the workspace ends. Storage is requested at the project.
start.scratch: Local storage outside the home: {{gb}} GB per workspace, e.g. for packages installed with pip or conda and /tmp. Files in the home do not count. Writing more ends the workspace; larger packages belong in the project's environment.
start.scratchNoStorage: Local storage: {{gb}} GB per workspace, without workspace storage including the home. Writing more ends the workspace.
start.deletes: On {{date}} its workspaces are deleted with all files; save what matters before or have the project extended.

envs.cpu: Workspace on the CPU with JupyterLab and VS Code. Up to 4 CPU cores and 8 GB RAM.
envs.cpu-gpukernel: Notebook on the CPU; the kernel “Python 3 (GPU)” starts on a GPU when needed. GPU kernels end after 5 min without execution, losing their variables.
envs.gpu: Whole workspace on a GPU with JupyterLab and VS Code. Waits until a GPU is free.

start.linkHint: The link opens this page with the current choice; nothing starts before “Start”.
start.unknownProject: The project “{{project}}” from the link is not one of your active projects with workspaces. The project's managers add members.
start.blockedProject: The project “{{project}}” from the link allows no environment, so nothing can be started there.
start.unknownEnv: The environment “{{env}}” from the link is not allowed in this project.
start.waiting: The workspace is starting, usually in less than a minute. It opens here once it is ready.
start.waitingGpu: The workspace waits for a free GPU, then starts. It opens here once it is ready.
start.gone: The workspace could not start. The list of active workspaces shows what is running; starting again reports the reason.
start.limits: Ends after {{idle}} without activity, after {{max}} at the latest.
start.building: The environment's image is being built from the Git repository. Workspaces can start once the build is done; this page updates by itself.
start.buildFailedTitle: The environment could not be built
start.buildFailed: Without a built image no workspace can start in this project. Those who manage the project can fix the repository in the project settings (Workspaces) and build again.
start.linkHintAuto: The link starts the workspace with this choice as soon as it is opened; when one is already running there, it opens that one.

empty.title: First a workspace project
empty.why: A workspace always runs in a project: the project brings the computing time, the storage and the environments allowed. There is no active project yet that a workspace can start in.
empty.noEnv_one: The project {{projects}} allows no environment, so nothing can be started there. Which environments a project allows is set by its budget and the people who administer the project.
empty.noEnv_other: The projects {{projects}} allow no environment, so nothing can be started there. Which environments a project allows is set by its budget and the people who administer the project.
empty.instant: The budget “{{budget}}” gives you one right away.
empty.onRequest: A project can be requested from the budget “{{budget}}”; it can be used once approved.
empty.noBudget: No budget in reach offers workspaces right now. Lecturers or administrators set up access to a budget; the people who administer an existing project can add you as a member.

release.title: Release times
release.hint: Idle time counts, not runtime: as long as something computes (a cell, a background thread with CPU or GPU load, a program in the terminal), the workspace keeps running. Empty fields take the budget's value, without one there the default. Shortly before the release a warning appears in JupyterLab. Changed times apply to workspaces started afterwards.

kinds.cpu: CPU – CPU workspaces and the notebook of “CPU + GPU kernel”
kinds.gpu: GPU – GPU workspaces and GPU kernels

release.budgetHint: The project chooses up to these values; empty fields = default. No upper bound only for GPU and only with the project's own GPUs (GPUs per class); the shared pool always has one.
release.budgetFromTree: The maximums are set by the budget in the budget tree.
release.idleBoth: Released after {{open}} without activity, without an open tab after {{closed}}

jobs.title: Batch jobs
jobs.intro: GPU jobs without a workspace: a command or a notebook runs in the project's environment, waits in the queue for a GPU and ends by itself. Listed are the own jobs; filtered by project, the project's managers see all of its jobs.
jobs.noProject: None of your projects allows batch jobs. The DHBW Cloud admins decide that.
jobs.name: Job
jobs.cancelMessage: “{{name}}” is cancelled. What the job wrote until then stays in the home.
jobs.outputHint: The end of the output, refreshed while the job runs. The whole output of every attempt is in the home under ~/jobs/{{name}}/.
jobs.noOutputYet: The job is still waiting; there is no output yet.

submit.title: Submit job
submit.intro: The job runs in the project's environment with the own home and ~/project-shared. Its output is also in ~/jobs/<name>/output-<attempt>.log. A preemptible job is ended when a workspace needs the GPU and starts again from the beginning afterwards.
submit.cliHint: pip install dhbw-cloud, then dhbw-cloud login with an API token.
submit.imagePending: The project's environment is being built; the job waits until it is ready.
submit.name: Name
submit.nameHint: Optional; also names the folder ~/jobs/<name>. Empty: the job's id.
submit.commandHint: Runs in a shell in the working directory.
submit.notebookHint: Path in the home; the notebook is run with papermill, the executed copy lands next to it.
submit.workingDirHint: Relative to the home; empty: the home.
submit.maxHoursHint: After that the job is ended. The time is reserved of the project's GPU budget; at most {{max}} h.
submit.errHours: More than 0 and at most {{max}} hours.

jobs.notAllowed: Batch jobs are not enabled in this project. The DHBW Cloud admins decide that.
jobs.notAllowedAdmin: Batch jobs are not enabled in this project.
jobs.noProjectAdmin: None of your projects allows batch jobs. Choose a project above to enable them.
